title: Ordinary derivative in an equation
parts: y′ = ky
The derivative of y equals a constant k times y.
note: The equation relates a function to its derivative.
wrong: The second derivative of y equals ky.

title: Initial condition
parts: y(0) = y₀
At time zero the solution has value y₀.
note: The subscript marks a starting value. y₀ itself need not be zero.
wrong: The derivative at time zero equals y₀.

title: Boundary conditions
parts: The solution is zero at the left endpoint
and one at the right endpoint.
example: For y″=0, the two conditions select y(x)=x.
note: Conditions at distinct endpoints are boundary conditions.
wrong: The slope is zero at x=0 and one at x=1.

title: Equilibrium solution
parts: The state y∗ makes the rate zero in the autonomous equation y′=f(y).
note: An equilibrium is a constant solution and need not be stable.
wrong: y∗ must be the largest possible value of y.

title: Heat equation
parts: ∂u/∂t
The rate of temperature change in time
= κ ∂²u/∂x²
equals κ times the second derivative in space.
example: A constant temperature has zero spatial curvature and zero time derivative.
note: Time has a first derivative and space has a second derivative.
wrong: The spatial rate equals κ times the second time derivative.

title: Separation of variables
parts: dy/g(y) = f(t) dt
Where g(y) is nonzero, collect y terms on one side and t terms on the other before integrating.
example: For y′=2y and y>0, integrating dy/y=2 dt gives ln y=2t+C.
note: Check constant solutions separately before dividing by g(y).
wrong: Every differential equation can be written this way.

title: Laplace transform
parts: ℒ{f}(s)
The integral of e to the power −st times f(t) from t=0 to infinity, when it converges.
example: For f(t)=1, ℒ{f}(s)=1/s for real s>0.
note: The transform gives a function of s.
wrong: The integral of f from zero to s without weighting.

title: Characteristic equation of an ODE
parts: r² + ar + b = 0
The equation for exponential rates r in y″+ay′+by=0.
example: For y″−3y′+2y=0 the roots are 1 and 2, giving eᵗ and e²ᵗ.
note: The roots give rates used to build solutions.
wrong: This gives the initial values of y and y′.
